signal: first-round pick (2024, 31st) AND three of three — the only free player with both
news: 1 Aug 2026, CBS Sports and ESPN: season-ending surgery on the PCL he hurt in week 4 of 2025. Recovery 6 to 12 months. Placed on season-ending injured reserve.|The nine games he played in 2025 were the same knee. The counterweight and the signal are the same injury.
bull: On paper he is the best free receiver in the league: a late first-rounder with a real role (53 targets, 5.9 a game, 10.3 yards a target in nine games) and only 2.6% of leagues own him.
bear: He will not play a down in 2026. And a player added off waivers can never be a keeper here, so there is no next-year payoff to bank either. An IR stash you cannot keep is a spot spent on nothing.
note: He is the reason this section exists and the reason it needs a news column. The arithmetic liked him more than any other name on the wire and the arithmetic could not see a knee. San Francisco's receivers took only 45% of the team's targets last season, the third smallest room in the league, and it fed three men. Moving up inside a small room is worth about half what it is worth on a spread team, so the room is a second reason against him on top of the knee.

signal: first-round rookie — the only free one
verdict: the cheapest lottery ticket on the page
news: 15 Aug 2026, Yahoo citing ESPN's Rich Cimini: "He was leapfrogged on the depth chart by Isaiah Williams." Fourth receiver behind Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Williams.|His preseason debut was 26 yards, playing with the backups.
bull: Of the first-round rookie receivers who sat behind an established number one, six of fifteen were startable in year one, and nine out-targeted the man ahead of them. Draft capital is the one receiver signal that has ever measured here, and it is free to hold.
bear: WR4 on a team whose WR1 is Garrett Wilson. Being fourth in the room in September is how most of the nine misses started, and the two of ours who were added mid-season after falling down a depth chart both stayed there.
note: 5.2% rostered. The odds column is blank for him on purpose: on this league's own in-season adds the first-round rookie is 0 for 6, which is far too few to mean anything. The Jets gave their receivers 60% of the targets and fed three. His signal is the one about THIS season: a first-round rookie paired with a returning target leader out-targeted him 9 times in 15, and 40% of those rookies were startable in year one.

signal: three of three on the screen, AND the only slot receiver in Denver's room - 57.8% of his routes from the slot at 10.0 yards deep
verdict: the best live screen on the wire
news: 9 Sep 2026, Heavy: the week-1 depth chart lists him third, behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle, with Marvin Mims starting ahead of him — the surprise of the sheet.|Sean Payton on him: "rarely does he have to leave his feet to make a clean catch." Sports Illustrated's Chad Jensen predicts a break-out as the number three who "will see the field often."|Mims is a deep threat and Bryant is a possession receiver, so they are not competing for the same snaps.
bull: He clears all three signals, he is healthy, he is 1.9% owned, and the coach who decides his snaps has spent a career feeding big possession receivers.
bear: He has to take the slot from TROY FRANKLIN, and that is the whole of it - no injury required and none sufficient. Sutton (81.5% wide, 13.3 deep) and Waddle (76.5%, 13.2) are boundary receivers who barely overlap him. What DOES cut against him: Waddle's arrival locks the boundary and squeezes Franklin (54.7% wide) inside, onto Bryant's own snaps. Franklin was 31st of 33 at 6.95 yards a target against Bryant's 8.04, so it is a fight Bryant can win on performance - but it is a fight.
note: The screen fires on a third of the players who clear it, and it fires at the same rate in September as in December. Denver's receivers took 61% of the targets and the team fed four of them — one of the wider rooms, which is where moving up the order pays most. Of the four names here his room and his health are both on the right side. And he does not need to out-target anybody to matter: among young receivers behind a returning team leader, 36% of the ones who became startable never passed the man ahead - and 13 of the 22 who DID pass him were still not startable.

signal: three of three, on four games
verdict: the same screen on a thinner base

bull: The late-2024 stretch is the only evidence on this page of a screened receiver actually producing at a startable rate, and he is the same age and the same role now.
bear: His three signals are computed on FOUR GAMES. Yards a target and targets a game are rates, and a rate off four games is the thinnest input on this page. He is also the one name here a third of the league already owns, so he is the least likely to still be free.
note: 33.9% rostered — much the highest of the four, which is its own information. Tampa Bay fed FIVE receivers and gave the room 67% of all targets — the most spread offence in the league. That is the single best room on this page to be promoted inside, and it is the half of his case that today's measurement improved. His rates still come off four games.
